trust_decision.summary: Tickets::getAllGrouped decides whether user-controlled text (status names, milestone headline, editor name, ticket type, project name) is HTML-escaped before it becomes the group 'label', which the kanban swimlane header prints raw with {!! !!}; it also builds the group 'id' that templates put into inline onclick JS strings.

landing_point.why: The summary names Tickets.php getAllGrouped on the Kanban board. The switch already escapes the sprint and parent-task branches (lines 776, 788), so the missing branches are easy to see next to them.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All fix hunks are in the one switch at app/Domain/Tickets/Services/Tickets.php:700-803. The program-board projectId branch (797-798) is reached through getProgramTicketTemplateAssignments (4143), a separate entry point, but it is the same function, not a second implementation.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about the label HTML. The group 'id' already goes through Blade {{ }} escaping in the onclick attributes (swimlane-row-header.blade.php:77-78, showAll.blade.php:65), so a solver can argue it is already escaped, even though HTML-entity escaping does not protect a JS string literal inside an event-handler attribute.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The label is deliberately printed raw because some branches embed markup: the type icon <i class='fa ...'> and the editor profileImage <div>, which the swimlane header strips with a regex. Escaping the whole label, or switching the template to {{ }}, breaks the icon and the avatar stripping. Separately, the list/table templates already print label with {{ }}, so escaping at the source double-escapes there (e.g. '&' shows as '&').

O6_input_shapes: status label name from project settings (stored serialized)
milestone headline and milestone status name (more-info string)
editor first/last name, plus an (int) cast on editorId inside the img src
ticket type free text appended after the icon markup
project name in the label, and the project name in the sortId used as group id (regex sanitized)

O7_producer.where: The status names come from project settings saved unescaped by Tickets::saveStatusLabels (app/Domain/Tickets/Services/Tickets.php:160-184, serialized at 184) and read back through getStateLabels (app/Domain/Tickets/Services/Tickets.php:100-102).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: groupBy=type: the group id defaults to strtolower(ticket type) with no sanitizing and goes into the inline onclick JS literal toggleSwimlane('...'). The fix sanitized only the projectId sortId. Type is free text in addTicket.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The id is HTML-escaped by Blade {{ }} in the template, and the report talks about the label, not the id.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; the sink is in app/Views/Templates/components/kanban/swimlane-row-header.blade.php:77-78 and app/Domain/Tickets/Templates/showAll.blade.php:65 (type free text: app/Domain/Tickets/Services/Tickets.php:2129)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: groupBy=milestone: groupColor = milestone->tags is passed through as group 'color'. The list templates escape it in style=; the kanban path does not use it. Recorded as a candidate only.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Colour is not a label, and the templates htmlspecialchars it (app/Domain/Tickets/Templates/showAll.blade.php:64).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a due-date bucket label or more-info that embeds a user-controlled value (e.g. a sprint or milestone name) without escaping
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: groupTicketsByDueDate is a separate producer of the same group shape that the switch comment's 'escaping boundary' does not cover, and it feeds the same raw sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getStatusBreakdownBySwimlane re-emits label/moreInfo; a variant that rebuilds the label from raw ticket fields
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a second @api producer of label/moreInfo for the same swimlane template.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: annotateTicketsWithStatusType on the program board could relabel status groups from per-project status names
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Program-board status grouping uses semantic types and per-project labels, which is a natural place to rewrite group labels.
